abstract: Web browsers now provide AI-generated news summaries for millions of users. Despite their popularity and influence, we lack a systematic understanding of how these systems transform news before people read it. Through a large-scale audit, we investigate the factual accuracy of browser-based AI summarizers and how they alter the political bias, negative affect, and journalistic writing quality of news. Drawing on 13,777 articles from 15 U.S. news outlets, we evaluate their 41,331 summaries generated by three leading AI-powered browsers: Google Chrome (Gemini), Microsoft Edge (Copilot), and Perplexity Comet. We find that browser-based AI summarizers are broadly accurate. Furthermore, they consistently transform news by attenuating ideological bias, partisan stances, negativity, anger, and fear, while increasing clarity and reducing personal tone. With some variations, these patterns hold across browsers, outlet ideologies, and topics. Our findings identify AI-powered browsers as a new class of editorial intermediaries that systematically reshape news, with implications for democratic discourse and AI governance.

ob.tldr: 基于15家美国新闻媒体的13,777篇文章生成的41,331条摘要，本文对Google Chrome（Gemini）、Microsoft Edge（Copilot）和Perplexity Comet三大AI浏览器进行系统性审计。研究发现AI浏览器摘要整体事实准确性较高，并系统性地减弱意识形态偏见、党派立场、负面情绪、愤怒与恐惧，同时提升清晰度、降低个人语气，跨浏览器、媒体倾向和话题均较为稳健。研究将AI浏览器界定为新型编辑中介，探讨其对民主话语与AI治理的影响。

title: AI-Powered Browsers Are Broadly Accurate News Summarizers That Reduce Political Bias and Negative Affect
title_zh: AI驱动浏览器：广泛准确的新闻摘要工具，可减少政治偏见与负面情绪
